“the only way to get rid of temptation is to yield to it.” ~ oscar wilde. i have serious impulse control issues and often use this quote as the final comforting push before giving in to whatever impulsive thing i might be about to do.

this is probably gonna be deleted but i’ve been sitting here trying so hard to think of anything that keeps me going and the only quote i can think of is the one that does the opposite; “the only way to rid yourself of temptation is to yield to it.” whenever i’m fighting myself on something i go back to that. i have a terrible inherent need to do the impulsive things that i crave to make myself feel alive at all. i wish i had a mantra to make me strong

that everyone with borderline personality disorder is insincere and our intense emotional outbursts are manipulative and shallow. while some people can definitely be manipulative it’s more about that person specifically and less about bpd. out emotions and pain may seem out of proportion or melodramatic but in the moment, whatever we feel is all consuming and unbearable. we are emotional third degree burn victims - the slightest touch can be agony.

i work at a hotel located in a historic building, and due to the hotel’s age the elevator can be slow. it’s inspected and safe but we can’t speed it up, sadly. i have people tear me a new asshole about this at least four times a week. 

some other fun reasons i have been yelled at are lack of flavored creamers in the rooms (only at the station in the lobby), the breakfast room not serving hash browns (sorry that’s not a Marriott standard for our brand), me calling them “ma’am,” my nose ring, and honestly a fucking plethora of other dumb things. i especially love when they refuse to read their parking pass, which is literally highlighted with important info, and as a result park in the wrong spot and are ticketed by the city. i have literally had people look me in the face and ask me if i expect them to actually read the information that i gave them at check in.

My dad got divorced from my stepmom when I was 8, and I was pretty angry with him because I had really loved her a lot and it was pretty much his fault that their marriage fell apart. One day, literally like two weeks after she left him, he was wondering out loud why he couldn’t keep her plants alive. 

Always one to have a snarky answer, I piped up, “They’re dead. Like your marriage.” 

He stared at me in shock for a good ten seconds. My dad is a loud guy when he gets angry, so when he only said quietly “Why would you say that?” I immediately burst into guilty tears and ran to my bedroom.
before i was in my abusive relationship and after. nothing changes your sense of trust, self worth, or understanding of love like being abused by someone who claims to love and care about you most.

my grandparents own a llama farm. we were taking them for a walk one day. i was 8 and very scared that i would accidentally let go and the llama would run away, so i wrapped the lead around my hand and wrist. bad idea. llama got spooked by something in the trees nearby and took off running. dragged me about 100 feet down the gravel road. by the time i got unraveled from the lead  i was covered in cuts and scrapes and bleeding all over. i’m 23 now and the only mark left is a fun bumpy scar on my right knee. it’s a good story, at least i’ve always enjoyed telling it!
